texts.preamble: Ram Krishan vs State Of Himachal Pradesh on 26 October, 2016 Author: Ajay Mohan Goel Bench: Ajay Mohan Goel In The High Court Of Himachal Pradesh, Shimla Cr. R. No. 16 of 2009. Reserved on: 21.10.2016. Decided on: 26.10.2016. Ram Krishan ....Petitioner. . Versus State of Himachal Pradesh ... Respondent. Coram The Hon'ble Mr. Justice Ajay Mohan Goel, Judge. Whether approved for reporting?1 No of For the petitioner. : Mr. M.S. Thakur, Advocate.
texts.facts: The case of the prosecution was that on 21.4.2004 . Food Inspector L.D. Thakur inspected the premises i.e. Sharma Sweets Shop, Rohru at about 2:00 p.m. and found the present petitioner conducting business of said sweet shop. The items which were kept for sale to the general public included "Laddu, Jalebi, Burfi and Samosas etc." etc. Food Inspector asked the of petitioner to produce P.F.A. licence issued in his favour for sale of food articles, as was required under Rule 50 of P.F.A. Rules, rt 1955, however, accused failed to produce any licence issued in his favour to conduct the abovementioned business for the years 2004-2005. Besides this, the sweets were kept uncovered exposed to rain, dust and flies. Accordingly, Food Inspector prepared a spot map which was duly signed by the accused and Food Inspector himself. Thereafter, Food Inspector placed documents of the accused before Chief Medical Officer, Shimla who was empowered to give written consent under Section 20 of the P.F.A. Act to launch prosecution against the accused. In this background, Food Inspector filed complaint against the accused under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of P.F.A. Act. 3. As a prima facie case was made out against the accused for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(II) read with Section 7(iii) of P.F.A. Act, 1954, accordingly notice of accusation was put to him to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Feeling aggrieved by the said two judgments passed by learned courts below, the accused has preferred the present revision petition.
texts.arguments: It has been further held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Janta Dal Vs. H.S. Chowdhury & others, 1992 (4) SCC rt 305 that the object of the revisional jurisdiction was to confer power upon superior criminal Courts a kind of paternal or supervisory jurisdiction in order to correct miscarriage of justice arising from misconception of law, irregularity of procedure, neglect of proper precaution or apparent harshness of treatment which has resulted on the one hand, or on the other hand in some undeserved hardship to individuals.
